confidence_note: This model (gradient boosting, chosen because it scored best of the two candidates tried) had backtested accuracy (52.5%) that was actually LOWER than simply always predicting the majority class (52.8%) on real held-out test data -- this model showed no real edge and underperformed even the trivial baseline. Treat any direction call from it with strong skepticism, not just mild caution -- it is not a case of 'close but unproven', it actively did worse.
price_confidence_note: This price forecast (linear regression, chosen because it scored best on real held-out test data) had error that was NOT statistically better than simply assuming tomorrow's price equals today's price (Wilcoxon signed-rank test on squared errors). Present the dollar figure as the model's best guess only -- do not imply it is a reliable forecast beyond the current price itself.
implied_volatility_note: implied_volatility_expected_range is a REAL, market-derived expected price RANGE (from CBOE's Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index, computed from actual USO options prices, same methodology as VIX) -- this describes how FAR price might move over the next period, NOT which direction. It's genuinely different information from the direction/price predictions above (this system's own model outputs) -- never conflate the two.
rolling_accuracy_note: Only 2 resolved live predictions so far (need at least 20 for a meaningful significance test). Raw accuracy so far: 0/2 (0.0%), but treat this as too small a sample to draw a real conclusion from yet.
cross_asset_consistency_note: The DXY prediction model does not yet have a real direction call to compare against (commonly because it's still in its data ramp-up period).
